title: Five arrangers, Ellington-like sound, and the trumpet section
summary: Albert says his band had original arrangements from several stylists, an Ellington-like instrumentation with two bass fiddles, and trumpet leads by Billy Douglas and Alvin Alcorn.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: See, in this band, we had five arranges. There was no one sound to the band. I mean, no. I don't feel that you copied. What? A set patent. Yeah, I don't think you copied anybody. It's a lot of variety in the band.

It's all original arrangements. Individual stylists. Well, I'll say this. We did copy a few numbers that are not recorded on here. In the same vein as Duke played, we used the same instrumentation and the same sound. Because the band was closely related, because this band has two bass fiddles. Al Holmes and Trini Johnson.
He swings with every note that trumpet plays. That's right. It must be Billy, huh? That's Billy.
Well, you have Billy, and then you have Alcorn and Arnie.

In this band? Yeah. Alvin Alcorn. Always? Well, until after I stopped. I was in the same room. Then at one time, there was a little fella named Sean Anderson, but he didn't last at all. He copied Billy Douglas' style.
